sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by impermeable cell-impermeant CA-Alexa488 (for Halo) or BG-Alexa488 (for SNAP) staining of live cells; all tagged receptors in the library were positively detected. No signaling or ligand-binding assay reported for the tagged construct.
sites.rationale: L2 explicitly states the tag is placed 'downstream the signal peptide sequence' with a 5x glycine linker; for ACVRL1 the signal peptide spans residues 1–21 (computed), so the junction is after residue 21 (G) and before residue 22 (D), the mature N-terminus. L3 (same paper) confirms cell-surface display by impermeable dye staining. The extracellular domain is 99 residues long (22–120), providing ample space before the TM helix at residue 121. Full-length hALK1 subcloned into pcDNA3.1 mUnc5b-SNAP/Halo backbone; Halo- or SNAP-tag fused N-terminally with a 5x glycine linker placed explicitly downstream of the signal peptide sequence, generating intact membrane-anchored receptor. Expressed in mammalian cells.

sources.claim: BMP/TGFβ receptors, including type I receptors (hALK1-ALK6, rALK7, and hALK2-R206H) and type II receptors (hACVR2A, hACVR2B, hBMPR2, and hTGFBR2) were, therefore, N-terminally fused with Halo- or SNAP-tags separated by a 5x glycine linker downstream the signal peptide sequence, to obtain the receptor library shown in Fig. 1c .
To this end, we initially coexpressed extracellularly tagged HA-ALK1 (wild type [WT], constitutively active Q201D, or kinase-dead K221R) together with myc-TβRIII.

literature_notes: All four ledger lines concern the same junction: the N-terminal extracellular position immediately after signal-peptide cleavage (after residue 21). L1, L2, and L3 are from the same publication (PMC9837045) and together constitute a validated, surface-confirmed insertion of Halo/SNAP tags at this exact site; L2 is cited as the primary evidence because it most explicitly states the position ('downstream the signal peptide sequence'). L4 (PMC8101464) independently reports an HA-tagged ALK1 described as 'extracellularly tagged' with no residue specified; topology derivation places it at the same junction. No ledger line supports any internal extracellular loop insertion or a C-terminal extracellular tag (the C-terminus is intracellular). No other_positions are reported because no ledger line describes a tolerated intracellular insertion or a function-abrogating insertion for ACVRL1.
